clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on apixaban initially presented with sudden mid-back pain after a flight, diagnosed as mechanical back pain and discharged. He re-presented 2 days later with more severe, burning mid-back pain, new hypoxia, and stiff calves; a CT aortogram ruled out aortic dissection and PE, and he was discharged with antibiotics for presumed infection. The next day, he presented for a third time with urinary retention, attributed to constipation and managed with catheterization and laxatives. The following day, he presented for the fourth time with headache, neck stiffness, vomiting, dramatically reduced lower limb coordination and power, and ataxic gait. This led to suspicion of hemorrhagic spinal pathology and cessation of apixaban. An MRI of the spine was performed, initially reported as thoracic syringomyelia, but later determined to be a spinal subdural haematoma. A repeat MRI one month later showed near complete resolution of the haematoma.
